html:
The first football World Cup was played in Montevideo, Uruguay, in July 1930. Uruguay hosted it and won it, beating Argentina 4 to 2 in the final.

FIFA, the world body of football, picked Uruguay because its team had won the Olympic football gold in 1924 and 1928, and because 1930 was the hundredth year of the country's first constitution. The Estadio Centenario was built for the tournament and named for that anniversary.

Only thirteen teams took part. The voyage from Europe took about two weeks by ship, and only four European teams made the trip: France, Belgium, Romania and Yugoslavia. FIFA's president Jules Rimet carried the trophy over, and it was later named after him.

From this small start the World Cup grew into the most watched sporting event on earth, held every four years except during the Second World War. South America took four of the first ten titles, and players such as Pelé made the tournament a global stage.
sum: The first football World Cup was played in Montevideo, Uruguay, in July 1930. Uruguay hosted it and won it, beating Argentina 4 to 2 in the final.
